email_script = '''
import smtplib
from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart
from email.mime.base import MIMEBase
from email.mime.text import MIMEText
from email import encoders
import os

msg = MIMEMultipart()
msg["From"] = "assistant@workspace.local"
msg["To"] = "bob@example.com"
msg["Subject"] = "Customer Report - Maya Chen (Orders ORD-6C71B1 & ORD-5B048F)"

body = """Hi Bob,

Please find attached the customer report for Maya Chen, covering orders ORD-6C71B1 and ORD-5B048F.

Summary:
- Order ORD-6C71B1: Delivered ($1,249.99)
- Order ORD-5B048F: Processing ($879.50)

Best regards,
Automated Report System"""

msg.attach(MIMEText(body, "plain"))

pdf_path = "docs/customer_report.pdf"
with open(pdf_path, "rb") as f:
    part = MIMEBase("application", "octet-stream")
    part.set_payload(f.read())
    encoders.encode_base64(part)
    part.add_header("Content-Disposition", f"attachment; filename=customer_report.pdf")
    msg.attach(part)

# Try sending via localhost SMTP
try:
    with smtplib.SMTP("localhost", 25, timeout=5) as server:
        server.sendmail(msg["From"], [msg["To"]], msg.as_string())
    print("Email sent successfully via localhost SMTP")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"SMTP localhost failed: {e}")
    # Save the email as .eml file as fallback
    eml_path = "docs/customer_report_email.eml"
    with open(eml_path, "w") as f:
        f.write(msg.as_string())
    print(f"Email saved as EML file at {eml_path}")
    # Also try sendmail
    try:
        ret = os.system(f'echo "{body}" | mail -s "Customer Report - Maya Chen" -A {pdf_path} bob@example.com 2>&1')
        if ret == 0:
            print("Email sent via mail command")
        else:
            print("mail command also failed")
    except:
        print("mail command not available")
'''
